purpose: Development corpus for T1/T2/T3 work. NOT evaluation data. Nothing measured against this corpus may be reported as a v2 result.
domain: Media asset publishing pipeline — transcoding, captions, storage tiers, licensing, CDN delivery.
disjointness: Chosen to share no topic with corpus-v2.json, whose domain is payments, auth, database migrations, deploys, CI, product search and observability. No v2 item could answer a dev query and no dev item could answer a v2 query.

authoring_record.note: Morphological pairs were written as a person would plausibly write and ask them, NOT selected for whether the porter stemmer unifies them. Some pairs are expected to be unrecoverable by stemming; that is a finding about the mechanism, not a defect in the corpus. The corpus is frozen at this commit and is not edited after a variant is run.

revisions.content: Caption jobs expire after 72 hours in the queue. An expired job is not retried automatically; the asset must be resubmitted through the ingest API.
Thumbnails fail to generate when the source has no keyframe in the first ten seconds. The pipeline falls back to a solid-colour placeholder rather than blocking publication.
Licence windows are approved by the rights desk, never by engineering. A window that opens without a recorded approval is a compliance incident, not a bug.
Assets migrate to cold storage tiers after 90 days without a playback request. Migration is reversible but takes up to four hours to restore.
The ingest API throttles uploads at 20 concurrent transfers per publisher. Exceeding the limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header the client is expected to honour.
Assets are published on the hour, not continuously. A publish that misses its slot waits for the next one; there is no expedite path.
The pipeline notifies subscribers when rendering completes, over a webhook with at-least-once delivery. Duplicate callbacks are normal and the receiver must be idempotent.
The per-asset encode work runs in transcode_worker.py. It is the only process permitted to write to the mezzanine bucket; anything else writing there is a bug.
An asset reaches AssetState.PUBLISHED only after captions, thumbnails and at least one playable rendition all exist. The state machine refuses the transition otherwise.
Players fetch /v3/assets/manifest for the rendition list. The v2 path is frozen and serves only clients pinned before the March cutover.
Every caption file carries a caption_track_id that is stable across re-encodes. Players cache by that id, so reusing one for different content silently serves the wrong subtitles.
Captions are stored as WebVTT. SRT is accepted at ingest and converted immediately; nothing downstream reads SRT.
To change an encode ladder, add the new rung alongside the old one, re-encode a sample of 50 assets, and compare VMAF before removing anything.
Edge caches hold manifests for 30 seconds and segments for a year. A bad manifest therefore clears quickly; a bad segment does not, and needs a purge.
Mezzanine files are the only copies kept at full quality. Deleting one means every future rendition is generated from an already-compressed source.
Territory restrictions are evaluated at playback, not at publication. An asset can be published globally and still be unplayable in most markets.
Thumbnail sprites are regenerated whenever the poster frame changes. The sprite sheet and the poster share a cache key, so they can never disagree.
Uploads arrive as a single multipart request. Resumable upload was evaluated and rejected: publisher sessions are short and the added state was not worth it.
Never re-encode from a delivery rendition. Generation loss compounds quickly and the result is not recoverable without the mezzanine.
The orchestration service is called flowreel. It owns job scheduling for every stage between ingest and publication.
The orchestration service is called assetline. It owns job scheduling for every stage between ingest and publication.
Audio is remuxed by the mux2 path for every asset.
Audio is remuxed by the mux2 path only for archive assets ingested before 2024. Everything newer goes through the current remuxer.
Caption turnaround is 48 hours from ingest for every title.
Caption turnaround is 6 hours from ingest for every title.
Playback start time is measured from the first manifest request, not from the user's tap. The gap between the two is a client concern and is not in our numbers.
The encode ladder tops out at 1080p. 4K was descoped in planning and no rung above 1080p exists in any profile.
